title: Looper Complexity and Line Distribution Comparison

repository.name: MumuTW/looper
repository.scope: Production Go cognitive complexity and physical line distribution only, compared with fork baseline a7a24238

summary.verdict: Current main is smaller and has a lower aggregate cognitive-complexity burden than the fork baseline, while its extreme tail remains concentrated in fixer and recovery orchestration.
strengths: Production Go lines fell from 116,884 to 105,952 (-9.4%) despite the production file count increasing from 210 to 221.
Total cognitive complexity fell from 52,178 to 47,287 (-9.4%); maximum complexity fell from 234 to 181.
Files over 1,000 lines fell from 32 to 24, and functions over complexity 100 fell from 17 to 12.
Issue #95 alone removed 110 production functions, 573 cognitive-complexity points, and 1,896 production Go lines.
risks: The current maximum remains very high: fixer Runner.ProcessClaimedItem is 181 and Runtime.runRecoveryPipeline is 178.
The count above complexity 50 is essentially flat versus the fork baseline (64 versus 63), so improvement is strongest in breadth rather than the extreme tail.
limitations: This is a metrics-only comparison; correctness, security, testability, and architectural authority were not reassessed.
gocognit and physical line counts are investigation signals, not proof that a function or file should be split.
The original working tree changed concurrently; all measurements use frozen immutable snapshots and exclude untracked files.

dimensions.name: Understandability
dimensions.summary: Complexity and size were measured, but no qualitative score is inferred from metrics alone.

dimensions.name: Maintainability
dimensions.summary: The distribution improved, but ownership and change-surface evidence was not re-audited.

findings.title: Characterize the remaining orchestration tail before further decomposition
findings.evidence: The aggregate and size distributions improved, but the extreme cognitive-complexity tail did not materially shrink.
findings.impact: Changes in orchestration-heavy paths may still require broad reasoning even though dead code and oversized-file counts declined.
findings.recommendation: Use impact and authority tracing before opening cleanup work; issue #271 already covers the recovery hotspot.

checks.summary: Measured 7,043 current and 7,550 baseline production Go functions.
Collected tracked source inventory for both immutable revisions.

items: Use issue #271 to trace recovery authority before reducing runRecoveryPipeline complexity.
Only open a fixer cleanup issue after mapping the impact surface of Runner.ProcessClaimedItem.
